newsitem.title: MEXICO: Former left-wing mayor slain in southern Mexican.
newsitem.headline: Former left-wing mayor slain in southern Mexican.

text.p: A former left-wing mayor of a town in the trouble-torn southern state of Guerrero and his wife were murdered by a group of armed gunmen, police and family sources said on Monday.
Guadalupe Valentino Lopez Carrasco, 50, of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), and his wife Nicasia Hernandez Petatan, 52, were shot in the head on Saturday.
Armed gunmen stopped the two grandparents close to the village of Xalpatlahuac, 120 miles (200 km) south of Mexico City, Lopez Carrasco's nephew Elvin Naves Flores said.
He said his uncle was travelling with his grandchildren, who were not harmed, and there were no signs of robbery.
Police said they had not found a motive for the murders of the couple, who had been working as teachers in the region.

Guerrero is a state often convulsed by intra-party violence, particularly between the PRD and local supporters of the Institutional Revolutionary Party. Rebels of the Popular Revolutionary Army emerged in the state last year.
Lopez Carrasco was PRD mayor of Malinaltepec, in the same mountainous region as Xalpatlahuac, between 1993 and 1996.
